newsitem.title: INDIA: Saudi airline protests India disaster speculation.
newsitem.headline: Saudi airline protests India disaster speculation.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Airlines protested on Wednesday over Indian press speculation over the cause of the world's deadliest mid-air collision as authorities urged relatives to come forward to identify 48 unknown bodies.
In a statement, Saudi Arabian Airlines said it had lodged a formal protest with India's director-general of civil aviation, objecting to media speculation about the cause of the crash.

"These reports deliberately ignore the fact that a judicial investigation is under way and serve only to cloud the complex issues involved in investigating a mid-air collision between two airliners," a spokesman for the airline said.

Early this week, search teams pulled from the wreckage the last of the bodies of the 349 people aboard the Saudi Arabian Airlines jumbo jet and the Kazakh cargo plane that collided in the sky near Delhi on November 12.
Officials said the bodies of 48 unidentified victims of the crash were decomposing in two Delhi hospitals.
"The bodies are rapidly decomposing and subsequent identification will not be possible," the Press Trust of India (PTI) quoted officials of the Airports Authority of India as saying.
Speculation over the causes of the crash ranged from outdated equipment at Delhi airport and language misunderstanding to pilot errors.
The Delhi High Court judge probing the crash has been given until February 15 to complete his inquiry.
Indian aviation officials have set up two control rooms in New Delhi to help provide relatives with information.
